Bug_Title: Methods with Spring proxying annotations should be public
Bug_Details:
Marking a non-public method @Async or @Transactional is misleading because Spring does not recognize non-public methods,
and so makes no provision for their proper invocation. Nor does Spring make provision for the methods invoked by the method it called.
Therefore marking a private method, for instance, @Transactional can only result in a runtime error or exception if the method is annotated as
@Transactional.
Bug_Explanation: The @Transactional annotation is supposed to be used with public methods to make sure that every method that is part of a method is part of the same transaction. However, in this code, the @Transactional annotation is used with a private method which is not allowed. This will lead to runtime errors when running the code.
Trigger_Explanation: This test case triggers the bug because it calls the showBug method which attempts to access a private method annotated with @Transactional. This results in a runtime error.
